descriptions.text: Unironically uses 'TikTok slang' in real-life conversations with actual human adults.
Will film a 15-second video of a tragedy or a car crash before even thinking about calling 911.
Has a secret finsta (fake Instagram) purely used to spy on people they claim to hate.
Their phone is constantly at 3% battery, yet they refuse to carry a charger and borrow everyone else's.
Spends 45 minutes trying to find the perfect meme to reply to a text that required a simple 'yes'.
Would genuinely suffer from physical withdrawal symptoms if they lost access to their phone for 2 hours.
Has matched with the same person on three different dating apps and got ghosted on all of them.
Takes a photo of their meal from six different angles while their friends starve in silence.
Leaves people on 'Read' for three days and then replies with 'Omg so sorry I just saw this!'.
Thinks having a curated aesthetic on Pinterest qualifies as having a real personality.
Falls deeply in love with a retail worker or a barista just because they smiled and said 'Have a nice day'.
Their type in partners can be best described as 'a walking project that needs heavy psychological rehabilitation'.
Will ignore 57 red flags just because the person has nice hair or a cool music taste.
Has broken up and gotten back together with the same toxic person more times than a fast-food menu changes.
Constantly complains about being single but rejects anyone who shows genuine interest because it's 'too easy'.
Will plan a whole wedding in their head after a first date that lasted exactly 45 minutes.
Convinced themselves that their toxic ex is 'the one that got away' instead of 'the one that thankfully left'.
Has a 'hiding spot' in their room for things they don't want a romantic partner to discover on a first visit.
Sends a screenshot of a text conversation to the wrong person—specifically the person the text was about.
Would definitely go on a reality TV dating show just to become a micro-influencer.
Buys a $7 iced coffee every morning but claims they will never buy a house because of 'the system'.
Will Venmo request a friend for $1.50 after splitting a cheap snack.
Has a gym membership they haven't used since the Obama administration but refuses to cancel it 'just in case'.
Owns three different credit cards and treats them like free money generators rather than crushing debt.
Would rather spend $40 on DoorDash delivery fees than walk two blocks to pick up the food themselves.
Always conveniently goes to the bathroom right when the restaurant bill arrives at the table.
Buys expensive concert tickets on a whim and then lives off instant ramen and tap water for a month.
Has a spreadsheet for their budget but stopped filling it out because looking at the numbers caused panic attacks.
Will spend $200 on a night out but will argue with a parking meter over 50 cents.
Their primary investment strategy is literally buying lottery tickets and crossing their fingers.
Will spray an aggressive amount of dry shampoo and cologne instead of just taking a 5-minute shower.
Has a pile of clothes on 'The Chair' that has developed its own micro-ecosystem and political system.
Would rather holding their breath and live in filth than take out a trash bag that is literally overflowing.
Has used the same bath towel for three weeks straight under the logic that 'I'm clean when I use it'.
Will cancel plans with friends solely because the idea of putting on pants with a zipper feels like too much work.
Their car interior looks like a recycling bin for fast-food bags and empty energy drink cans.
Has eaten leftovers that smelled slightly questionable just because they didn't want to cook anything new.
Will text someone who is in the exact same house just to avoid walking up a flight of stairs.
Hasn't changed their bed sheets since the last time they had a romantic prospect over—months ago.
Would rather drive around a parking lot for 15 minutes than park further away and walk for 30 seconds.
Has actively practiced their 'fake corporate phone voice' to sound like a functioning member of society.
Sends Slack or Teams messages at 11:00 PM just so their boss thinks they have a work ethic.
Steals an absurd amount of office supplies, snacks, and coffee pods from the company breakroom.
Has definitely cried in a corporate bathroom stall or a parked car during a lunch break.
Their entire professional identity is based on buzzwords like 'synergy', 'touch base', and 'circle back'.
Will schedule a 1-hour meeting that could have easily been a three-word text message.
Has 'Open to Work' on LinkedIn but clears their schedule the second a recruiter actually reaches out.
Spends 80% of their working hours looking at flights or online shopping on a secondary monitor.
Nods aggressively during business meetings while having absolutely no clue what the company actually sells.
Would gladly sell out their closest coworker for a 2% salary raise and a slightly bigger desk.
Always insists on playing DJ in the car or at a party, only to skip every song after 30 seconds.
Takes one shot of cheap tequila and suddenly speaks with a fake British accent for the rest of the night.
Will Irish-exit (disappear without saying goodbye) from a bar at 11:00 PM to go home and eat shredded cheese over the sink.
Suggests going out for 'just one quiet drink' and ends up crying in a fast-food parking lot at 4:00 AM.
Vapes so aggressively and constantly that they look like a broken steam engine from the 19th century.
Will aggressively suggest taking shots, but then hypes everyone else up while secretly pouring theirs into a nearby plant.
Spends the entire party sitting on the couch scrolling through TikTok, then posts a story captioning it 'Best night ever!'.
Will ruin the entire vibe of a pre-game by trauma-dumping about their childhood memories out of nowhere.
Always 'forgets' their wallet when going out but promises to 'Venmo you tomorrow' (they never do).
Attempts to do a backflip or a split on the dance floor and pulls a muscle so badly they need medical attention.
Diagnoses themselves with 4 different rare psychological conditions after watching two 30-second TikTok videos.
Buys a $12 green juice made of grass and celery dust, convinced it is actively reversing 10 years of terrible lifestyle choices.
Will look up a mild headache on WebMD and immediately start drafting a last will and testament on their notes app.
Tries a new diet for exactly 36 hours and acts like an insufferable, enlightened cult leader to everyone else.
Owns an expensive water bottle that tracks their hydration, but uses it mostly to hide iced coffee or wine.
Claims to have a severe food allergy to sound interesting at restaurants, but will happily eat the exact same food when drunk.
Spends $300 on vitamins and supplements that sit untouched in a cabinet until they expire.
Will complain about being chronically exhausted while drinking a giant energy drink at midnight.
Claims that 'nature is my therapy' but gets a massive panic attack the second a medium-sized bug flies near them.
Refuses to take a standard ibuprofen for a fever, opting instead for a weird crystal or a specialized tea that smells like wet dog.
Will deliberately post a group photo on social media where they look incredible, even if everyone else's eyes are closed.
Holds a grudge over a board game argument or a minor text slight that occurred during the Obama administration.
Will aggressively clear their throat or sigh loudly instead of politely asking someone to move out of the way.
Unfollows people on Instagram just to see if they notice and follow up with a 'hey, is everything okay?' text.
Will stalk an enemy's LinkedIn profile using 'Private Mode' like a highly trained corporate spy.
Leaves an empty toilet paper roll on the holder and just balances a new roll precariously on top of it.
Will reply to an incredibly long, emotional message with a single thumbs-up emoji response.
Remembers exactly who didn't wish them a happy birthday and secretly plots to do the same when their time comes.
Will mute a group chat because people are talking too much, then get mad when plans are made without them.
Borrows a piece of clothing, wears it to death, and returns it months later smelling like a completely different household.
Knows the entire romantic history and chart performance of Taylor Swift but doesn't know their own bank account balance.
Listens to true crime podcasts about gruesome serial killers to 'relax' and fall asleep at night.
Bases 90% of their political and social beliefs on infographics posted by meme accounts.
Will quote lines from 'The Office' or 'Friends' as if it's original comedy they invented themselves.
Still acts like their Hogwarts House assignment is a definitive and crucial psychological profile.
Watched one Formula 1 documentary on Netflix and now acts like a mechanical engineer and a racing expert.
Will defend a multi-millionaire celebrity online against random strangers as if it's their biological mother.
Has a Pinterest board dedicated to a lavish mansion lifestyle they will realistically never afford.
Is unironically convinced that retro gaming or buying vinyl records counts as having a deep, complex personality.
Will re-watch the same comfort TV show for the 14th time instead of starting a highly recommended 2-hour movie.
Buys vintage clothes at thrift stores, marks up the price by 300%, and calls it an 'eco-friendly fashion curation business'.
Acts like drinking their coffee black makes them tougher and more mature than everyone else in the room.
Will judgingly look at your shopping cart at the grocery store if it contains too many processed snacks.
Constantly brags about 'not owning a TV' while spending 9 hours a day staring at a phone screen.
Tells everyone they are 'doing a social media detox' via an incredibly long post across all social media platforms.
Unironically believes that people are intimidated by them, when in reality, people just find them incredibly exhausting.
Will use the phrase 'everything happens for a reason' to someone who just experienced a horrific, life-ruining event.
Acts like reading non-fiction self-help books makes them inherently superior to people who read for actual fun.
Will lecture you about the environment while ordering 4 plastic packages from Amazon every single week.
Thinks that traveling to another country for two weeks completely re-wired their soul and made them a citizen of the universe.
Will spend 35 minutes analyzing the punctuation of a text message that just says 'Ok'.
Is convinced that a coworker hates them because they didn't say 'good morning' with enough enthusiasm.
Replays an embarrassing conversation they had in 2016 in their head while trying to fall asleep tonight.
Will check if the front door is locked four separate times, walk away, and still worry about it all night.
Apologizes for apologizing too much, creating an infinite loop of social awkwardness.
Will read an entire restaurant menu online three days before going out because making a choice under pressure scares them.
Convinced that every minor physical symptom is the indicator of an extremely rare and terminal medical anomaly.
Drafts a text message in their Notes app, edits it three times, and then decides not to send it at all.
Thinks that everyone in the room is looking at them and judging their outfit, when in reality, everyone is just looking at their phones.
Will create a worse-case scenario matrix in their head for a completely normal, low-stakes situation.
Will scream profanities at a grandmother blocking traffic, but immediately acts polite if they make eye contact.
Needs to turn down the car radio entirely just so they can 'see better' while parallel parking.
Treats the highway speed limit like a casual suggestion and tailgates people like a professional race car driver.
Has zero sense of direction and will confidently drive 20 miles in the wrong direction because 'GPS feels wrong'.
Uses their blinker exactly 0.5 seconds after they have already started turning the steering wheel.
Their driving style is so chaotic and aggressive that being their passenger requires signing an unwritten life insurance waiver.
Will panic and miss their highway exit, then proceed to cut across three lanes of traffic to save 2 minutes.
Gets into a screaming match with an inanimate object, like a malfunctioning parking garage ticket machine.
Refuses to ever be the one who drives on road trips, but sits in the passenger seat critiquing every single turn.
Their car has a collection of mysterious dents and scratches that they claim 'just appeared overnight'.
Will eat a slice of pizza starting from the crust end like a literal psychopath.
Puts ketchup on high-quality steak or sushi, deeply offending anyone with taste buds.
Will double-dip their chip into the communal guacamole after taking a massive bite.
Takes the last slice of pizza or cake without asking, leaving a empty box in the fridge to mock everyone.
Cooks fish or burns popcorn in the office microwave, causing a localized evacuation of the building.
Chews their food so loudly that it sounds like a horse walking through heavy mud.
Will steal a single fry or a bite of food from your plate while saying 'I don't want to order anything, I'm not hungry'.
Orders a massive, overly complicated custom meal at a restaurant and then complains that it tastes weird.
Puts an empty milk carton back in the fridge just so they aren't the one who has to throw it away.
Uses a metal fork on a non-stick Teflon pan, scratching it to pieces without a single care in the world.
Will look at a sign that says 'Wet Paint' and immediately touch it with their bare hand to check.
Laughs at a highly inappropriate moment during a serious or solemn movie scene.
Can remember a random lyric from a 2000s pop song but forgets the name of the person they met 30 seconds ago.
Will buy a highly specific gadget (like an egg poacher) used once, then stores it in the abyss of a cabinet forever.
Sets 14 different alarms on their phone at 5-minute intervals, only to sleep through all of them.
Walks into a room with absolute purpose, forgets why they came in, stares at the wall, and walks out.
Will tell a story that takes 20 minutes to finish, only for the punchline to be completely uninteresting.
Has a 'junk drawer' containing 4 dead batteries, 12 mystery keys, a broken pen, and a receipt from 2019.
Will aggressively hit the crosswalk button 12 times, convinced it makes the light change faster.
Still opens their mail with their bare hands like a raccoon tearing into a garbage bag.
Stares into an open fridge for 5 minutes hoping that new, gourmet food has miraculously spawned since they checked 10 minutes ago.
Will put on a completely new outfit just to go to the grocery store for 10 minutes, treating the aisle like a runway.
Answers a rhetorical question seriously, creating a heavy, awkward silence over the entire room.
Will read the plot summary of a movie on Wikipedia while actively watching the movie next to you.
Lies about having seen a classic movie just to avoid the exhausting 'Omg you haven't seen it?!' conversation.
Will wave back at someone who was actually waving at the person standing directly behind them.
Keeps the plastic protective film on electronic devices until it naturally peels off and looks disgusting.
Will try to push a door that clearly and boldly says 'PULL' in high-contrast lettering.
Has definitely Google-searched their own name in incognito mode just to see if they are internet-famous yet.
Would definitely survive an actual horror movie scenario purely because they are too lazy or stubborn to investigate the weird noise in the basement.
